texts.facts: 2. At the outset, it must be mentioned that initially, the present suit was filed as non-commercial suit before the concerned Court of Ld. Additional District Judge, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. It may also be noted that initially, the suit was filed against the defendant, who was arrayed as 'Ashok Kumar' on the basis of 'John Doe' principle as applicable in India and subsequently, after execution of local commission in pursuant to relevant Court's order(s), the plaintiff got substituted the defendant nos. 1 and 2 in place of previous defendant/Ashok Kumar (John Doe) and placed on record Amended Memo of Parties. BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE: 4. The case of the plaintiff, as set out in the plaint, in brief is as under:- 4.1 The plaintiff is a limited partnership organized under the laws of Netherlands and got instituted the present suit through constituted attorney namely Mrs. Meena Bansal, who has been duly authorized by the plaintiff to institute, sign, verify and pursue the present suit. 4.2 It is stated that the plaintiff is engaged in manufacturing, sale and distribution of large variety of goods including clothing, footwear, athletic shoes, boots, bags of all kinds, sporting goods, watches and other timing devices, eye-wear, including sunglasses and protective eye-wear for the practice of sports, consumer electronic products, sports balls, golf equipment and other allied/ related products [hereinafter referred to as the 'said goods and business']. 4.3 Further, it is stated that the name of the plaintiff changed various times including recent change from M/s Nike International Limited to M/s Nike Innovate CV and the term 'plaintiff' includes 'the plaintiff and its predecessors'. 4.4 As per detailed history of adoption and expansion of plaintiff' trade mark/ label mentioned in Para no.4 of the plaint, it is claimed, inter alia, that Nike, originally known as Blue Ribbon Sports (BRS), was founded by Bill Bowerman and Phil Knight in Oregon in 1964. In the year 1971, the plaintiff became Nike Inc. and Jeff Johnson established company name 'Nike' which came from the name of Greek Goddess of Victory and also in the same year, Carolyn Davidson designed the Swoosh, depicted Nike Innvoate C V vs Pintu Sharma on 24 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129051222/ 2 as , in relation to its goods and business. Further, it is stated that Ilie Nastase became the first athlete to sign an endorsement contract with the plaintiff in the year 1972 and in the year 1984, the plaintiff signed Michael Jordan. In the year 1988, the slogan 'Just Do It' was coined and adopted by the plaintiff for its goods and business. In the year 2014, the Nike brand is valued $19 billion, which increased manifold and reached to $30 billion in the year 2017 and Nike brand remains no.1 brand in the world in apparels category. The plaintiff employs 58000 people worldwide. 4.5 Further, ever since its bonafide adoption of the trade mark NIKE in the year 1971, the plaintiff has subsequently been using the formative NIKE marks word per se & and in stylized manner in conjunction with other marks/words and Swoosh device in relation to its said goods and business in the course of Trade, which have been created and are being created over a period of time, viz. Nike, Nike Golf, Nike Pro, Nike+, Nike Skateboarding, Nike Bauer, Swoosh Device etc. which are depicted and reproduced as - , , and . [hereinafter referred to as 'said trademarks/ lables'] 4.6 Thus, it is claimed that ever since its inception, the plaintiff has been honestly & bonafidely, continuously, commercially, openly and to the exclusion of others, uninterruptedly and in the course of trade and as proprietor thereof, using its said trademarks/ labels in relation to its said goods and business and carrying on its said goods and business thereunder and have built up a worldwide and globally valuable trade, goodwill and reputation thereunder and have acquired proprietary rights therein. Thus, the plaintiff has claimed itself to be owner and proprietor of the said trademarks, which are stated to be registered, valid and subsisting as on date in favour of the plaintiff and details thereof have been given in Para No.7 of the amended plaint. 4.7 It is further claimed that Copyrights involved in the plaintiff' said trademarks/ labels are original artistic works within the meaning of Indian Copyright Act, 1957 and the plaintiff is the owner and proprietor thereof. The plaintiff has been dealing with the said Copyrights in the course of trade in relation to its said goods and business inter-alia within the meaning of Section 14 of the Copyright Act. 4.16 It is stated in the last week of February 2020, the plaintiff came across impugned goods of the defendants under the impugned Trade Mark/Label in New Delhi Area. The suit was accompanied with applications - one under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 CPC and another under Order XXVI Rule 9 CPC seeking ex parte ad interim injunction and ex parte order for appointment of local commissioner to visit and search the premises of the defendant. After hearing counsel of the plaintiff, the said applications were allowed, vide common order dated 17-03-2020 passed by Ld. Predecessor of its Court, thereby granting ex parte ad interim injunction in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant and two Local Commissioners were also appointed to visit and search the premises of the defendants with certain conditions as mentioned therein. As already noted above, subsequent to execution of local commission, the plaintiff had moved an application for substitution of name of John Doe entity with the name of the defendants, which was allowed, vide order dated 01-06-2022, passed by Ld. Predecessor of the Court. 7. At this juncture, it may also be noted that the present case was received by this Court on 18-10-2022, as already noted above in Para no.2, and an application under Order VI Rule 17 CPC was moved on behalf of the plaintiff seeking amendment of the suit, thereby enhancing specified value to be above Rs.3 lacs, so as to bring the present suit within the ambit of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, in view of the directions of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Vishal Pipes Limited (supra). 8. Since the defendants were still to be served,the notice of the aforesaid application along with copy of entire paper book were directed to be issued to them. However, since the defendants could not be served through ordinary mode of service, they were served through substituted mode of service by way of publication in daily newspapers - The Statement (English edition) and Dainik Jagran (Hindi Edition), both dated 24-2-2024, in terms of order dated 09-01-2024 passed by this Court, while allowing the application under Order V Rule 20 CPC of plaintiff for substituted service. Since despite being served through publication in aforesaid newspapers, none had appeared on behalf of defendants, therefore, they were proceeded against ex parte, vide order dated 04-06-2024, passed by this Court. 9. The aforesaid amendment application was also allowed and the plaintiff was directed to file requisite deficient Court Fee on record due to enhancement of valuation of the suit, vide order dated 21-8-2024, passed by this Court. 11. In support of its case, the plaintiff has examined only one witness i.e. its AR namely Mrs. Meena Bansal as PW1. After the closure of PE, ex parte final arguments were heard. 13. It may be noted here that during the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel of plaintiff made statement to give up prayers/reliefs as prayed in Prayer Clause Nos. 37(b) and 37(d) of the amended plaint regarding restraining the defendants from disposing off or dealing with their assets and rendition of accounts of profit respectively. Accordingly, the plaintiff was permitted to give up the said reliefs, vide order dated 28-10-2024.
texts.arguments: The said trademarks of the plaintiff are enforceable within the ambit of the Copyright Act 1957, as well as by virtue of India's membership to the Berne Convention, the Universal Copyright Convention and the International Copyright Order 1991. 4.8 It is stated that the plaintiff maintains the highest standard of quality in relation to its goods and business under the said Trade Marks/Labels/Trade Name. The plaintiff invests heavily in R & D and its products are known for their highest standards of quality, safety, innovation and reliability and there is an ever-increasing demand, therefore. 4.9 Further, it is averred that the plaintiff operates in more than 160 countries around the globe and directly or indirectly employs nearly one million people through suppliers, shippers, retailers and other service providers. At the end of fiscal year 2017, the plaintiff' affiliate businesses contributed approximately $5 billion of company's $30 billion in revenue. It is also claimed that the plaintiff has received a number of awards and have been widely recognized and details of awards have been given Nike Innvoate C V vs Pintu Sharma on 24 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129051222/ 3 in Para no.14 of the amended plaint. 4.10 The plaintiff has also got domains name registered in its favour, viz. www.nike.com and www.nikeinc.com [hereinafter referred to as the said domain name/ website] and the plaintiff is also carrying on its business activities under the said trademarks on the internet through its said websites which are stated to be interactive in nature. It is stated that the said trademark NIKE forms an essential and distinguishable part of the said domain name, which contains extensive information about the goods and services provided by the plaintiff under said trademarks/ labels and has large number of hits and viewership. 4.11 Further, it is the case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff has regularly and continuously been promoting its said trademarks/labels and goods and business thereunder through extensive advertisements, publicity, promotions and marketing and has been making research and the plaintiff has been spending enormous amounts of money, efforts, skills and time thereon. The plaintiff has been doing so through various means and modes including through the visual, print and electronic media and all of which have tremendous reach, visibility, distribution, availability and circulation world over including in India. 4.12 Hence, it is stated that on account of its good quality and standards of manufacturing and untiring efforts in advertising and marketing, the products of the plaintiff under the said trade marks/ labels have become distinctive and have acquired secondary significance with the plaintiff and plaintiff's said goods and business thereunder. Further, the purchasing public, the trade and industry at large worldwide and in India identify, distinguish and associate the plaintiff said goods under the said trademarks/labels with the plaintiff and from the plaintiff's source and origin alone and regard them as high quality products exclusively as that of the plaintiff. It is further claimed that the said trademarks/ labels are well known trademarks within the meaning of Section 2 (1) (zg) of the Trade Marks Act and have acquired enviable reputation and goodwill across the globe including India. 4.13 It is further stated that the plaintiff's said trademarks/ labels as well as the goods & businesses thereunder have a very strong presence in India and are commercially available in India including within the jurisdiction of this Court. In addition thereto, the plaintiff enjoy trans-border reputation and users of its said trademarks in relation to its said goods and business as extending into India. 4.15 It is alleged that the defendants are engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing, trading, selling, offering for sale, soliciting and marketing of readymade garments, apparels, clothing, sports-wear, Shoes, footwear, boot, sports related accessories, and other allied/related products and Tags, labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories, machineries and allied and cognate items Nike Innvoate C V vs Pintu Sharma on 24 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129051222/ 4 [hereinafter referred to as the 'impugned goods and business'] and have adopted and started using the NIKE [with or without SWOOSH DEVICE), DRI-FIT, FLYKNIT, NIKE AIR [hereinafter referred to as the "impugned trademarks/labels] in relation to his impugned goods and business. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff' caused an inquiry in the market, which revealed that the defendants had just about in the Month of February 2020 adopted and started using and soliciting the impugned Trade Marks/Labels in relation to their impugned goods in New Delhi Area. The defendants are not only making the retail sales but are also supplying the impugned goods bearing the impugned Trade Mark/Label to various other dealers/shopkeepers/retailers including in New Delhi area, who are making the clandestine and surreptitious sales thereof to the unscrupulous traders and manufacturers of the counterfeit products of the plaintiff under the said Trade Mark/Label in the markets of New Delhi Area viz. Connaught Place, Sarojini Nagar, Naraina, Gole Market, Mandir Marg and adjoining areas, etc. 4.17 Thus, it is alleged that the defendants have dishonestly and malafidely adopted impugned trademarks/ labels NIKE [with or without SWOOSH DEVICE), DRI-FIT, FLYKNIT, NIKE AIR, which are visually, structurally identical and/or deceptively and confusingly similar to the registered trademarks/labels of plaintiff NIKE [with or without SWOOSH DEVICE), DRI-FIT, FLYKNIT, NIKE AIR in relation to same goods and business, thereby causing confusion and deception amongst the unwary purchasing public and traders by making them believe that the origin of those goods are the plaintiff. It has been averred that by doing so, the defendants are not only damaging the reputation and goodwill of the plaintiff by passing off its substandard products as that of the plaintiff, but, are also causing financial loss to the plaintiff by reaping unfair advantage of the repute and distinctive character of the trademarks of the plaintiff. 4.18 Counsel of plaintiff has advanced the following arguments:- 15.1 Ld. Counsel of plaintiff has argued that the entire testimony of PW-1 has remained unchallenged and un-rebutted from the side of defendants and therefore, the plaintiff is entitled to the decree, as prayed for. In support of his submissions, Ld. Counsel also relied upon the documents [Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/8 and Ex.PW1/B.] 15.2 Further, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel of plaintiff that the trademarks/labels NIKE are well known trademarks/ labels of the plaintiff and are registered in India under the provisions of Trade Marks Act in favour of the plaintiff, which are valid and subsisting till date. Further, the art works involved in the said trademarks/ labels are original artistic works and the plaintiff hold copyright therein. Further, it is submitted that the plaintiff spends huge amount of money in advertising and promotion of its products and said marks enjoy a huge goodwill and reputation in business community and amongst public in general in India and across the world. 15.3 Further, he submitted that the use of impugned trade marks/labels as adopted by the defendants, which are identical and/ or confusingly or deceptively similar to Nike Innvoate C V vs Pintu Sharma on 24 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129051222/ 7 the registered trademarks of the plaintiff, not only amount to committing fraud upon the plaintiff but also upon the unwary general public, due to which the plaintiff suffer huge monetary loss and its goodwill and reputation are also at stake and therefore, he urged that the suit may be decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, thereby restraining the defendants and all others acting for and on their behalf from using the said impugned trade-marks/ labels. ANALYSIS & CONCLUSION: Therefore, in view of the law as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in cases titled as "Banyan Holding (P) Ltd. v. A Murali Krishna Reddy & Anr." reported as 2009 SCC OnLine Del 3780; "World Wrestling Entertainment, Inc. v. Reshma Collection & Ors." reported as 2014 (60) PTC 452 (Del.) (DB); and "Burger King v. Tekchand", reported as 2018 (76) PTC 90 (Del.), the Court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiff has been able to satisfy the test of purposeful availment of the plaintiff' goods under the trademarks / labels within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court, as stipulated in the said judgments delivered by Hon'ble Delhi High Court. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as "Renaissance Hotel Holdings Inc. v. B. Vijaya Sai & Ors" , reported as MANU/SC/0066/2022, has laid down law with respect to infringement of trade mark, to quote:- 43. The legislative scheme is clear that when the mark of the defendant is identical with the registered trade mark of the plaintiff and the goods or services covered are similar to the ones covered by such registered trade mark, it may be necessary to prove that it is likely to cause confusion on the part of the public, or which is likely to have an association with the registered trade mark. Similarly, when the trade mark of the plaintiff is similar to the registered trade mark of the defendant and the goods or services covered by such registered trade mark are identical or similar to the goods or services covered by such registered trade mark, it may again be necessary to establish that it is likely to cause confusion on the part of the public It has been held that the essentials of a passing off action with Nike Innvoate C V vs Pintu Sharma on 24 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129051222/ 9 those in respect of an action complaining of an infringement of a registered trade mark, cannot be equated. It has been held that though an action for passing off is a Common Law remedy being an action for deceit, that is, a passing off by a person of its own goods as those of another; the action for infringement is a statutory right conferred on the registered proprietor of registered trade mark for the vindication of the exclusive rights to the use of the trade mark in relation to those goods. It has further been held that if the essential features of the trade mark of the plaintiff has been adopted by the defendant, the fact that the get-up, packing and other writing or marks on the goods or on the packets in which he offers its goods for sale show marked differences, or indicate clearly a trade origin different from that of the registered proprietor of the mark, would be immaterial in case of infringement of the trade mark, whereas in the case of a passing off, the defendant may escape liability if he can show that the added matter is sufficient to distinguish its goods from those of the plaintiff. 47. Further, our own Hon'ble High Court in the case titled as 'Shaw Wallace & Co. Ltd. & Anr. v.
